context.title: Silicon Valley DSA — November 3, 2026 California general election voter guide

labels.label: Endorsed
labels.description: endorsements are approved by a 75% vote by the Chapter and entail a significant commitment of Chapter resources, time, and energy.

labels.label: Recommended
labels.description: Recommendations are approved by a majority of the Chapter only

subject.title: Governor of California

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We recommend no candidate in this race. Xavier Becerra has run a typical California Dem™ campaign: lots of words, few promises, and the eternal slogan of ‘I’m Not the Republican.’ Becerra will win the governorship with about 61% of the vote in November, will get sworn into office in January, and will spend the next four years governing like Newsom. At least he won’t use this office as a springboard for a presidential campaign…"

subject.title: Lieutenant Governor of California

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "No recommendation. Fiona Ma has served as a good treasurer of the state of California for eight years and will be a good lieutenant governor. Enough said."

subject.title: California Secretary of State

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend voting for Shirley Weber. Weber's long record of civil service began in academia where she founded the Africana studies department at SDSU (which she chaired for 40 years) and served as the president of the San Diego Board of Education for 8 years. In the State Assembly she continued to advocate expanding opportunities for higher education, while fighting for the creation of the CA Reparations Task Force (the first such statewide committee in the country). Secretary of State Weber has been instrumental in expanding voting rights, reversing disenfranchisement, and redistricting through the development of CA Prop 50."

subject.title: California Controller

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We recommend no candidate for Controller. The incumbent Malia Cohen is not in danger of losing. She is endorsed by establishment politicians and many unions, and has a war chest of large donations from PACs and the investor class. While Cohen previously supported targeted divestment in her role as commissioner of SFERS, she has yet to take any action on Tesla divestment from CalPERS, despite mounting pressure from the public. Her boilerplate talking points on affordability ring hollow as she puts in minimal effort to tackle those issues."

subject.title: California Treasurer

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We recommend no candidate in this race. Eleni Kounalakis is a protégé of Hillary Clinton and a real estate heiress. We see no reason to support a corporate-aligned moderate to oversee the state’s accountants."

subject.title: Attorney General of California

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We recommend no candidate in this race. While Bonta did lead the fight to ban for-profit prisons and immigration centers in California, and has been decent in his opposition of the tactics of DHS and ICE, we want more from him. The Housing Justice Team which he created, has shown potential by delivering protections to tenants and accountability for local governments and landlords alike who violate state housing laws, but he has dropped the ball on SB-79 housing issues that have severely impacted multiple cities in the Bay Area. And not only did he fail to prevent the Paramount-Warner merger that will cost Californian jobs and erode civil rights for all Americans, he has also failed to investigate rights violations of student protesters at UCLA and across the state. We believe he would be a better choice than his Republican opponent Michael Gates, but Bonta’s record falls entirely short of us considering a recommendation."

subject.title: California Insurance Commissioner

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend voting for Jane Kim. While the other Democrat in the race is beholden to the special interests of corporations and real estate PACs, Kim is primarily funded by small contributions from individuals. Endorsed by Bernie Sanders, more labor unions than any other candidate (including SEIU-CA, UHW, CTA, CFT, UAW), and the Working Families Party, Kim is the only viable candidate calling for material change in insurance policy. Kim’s platform aims to replace forms of for-profit insurance with state-run programs that would provide affordable, available insurance for all, including a public option of auto insurance and a plan for Medicare for Kids."

subject.title: California State Board of Equalization, District 2

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Sally Lieber. We have backed Lieber in her multiple campaigns over the last few years because we know she is a champion of California residents. Her continued presence on the Board of Equalization means a continued vote for fair and progressive taxation policy."

subject.title: California Superintendent of Public Instruction

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Richard Barrera. We feel comfortable with a guy who has a good amount of experience managing San Diego’s schools who has won the backing of the state’s teachers. In comparison, Shaw is a post-Covid, right-winger backed by the Republican Party and anti-trans activist Riley Gaines. This is not a serious person who can handle the serious problems facing California public education."

subject.title: US House of Representatives, California District 14

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Aisha Wahab for a full House term. The former state senator has a long record of public service and progressive advocacy, pounding the pavement for Measure A and being a warrior for foster youth. A champion of single-payer healthcare, the repeal of Citizens United, anti-racist legislation, and the expansion of rent control, she has earned a number of progressive endorsers. These include: US Representatives Pramila Jayapal (WA-7), Greg Casar (TX-35), and Maxwell Frost (FL-10); the CA Working Families Party; and many unions, including SEIU-CA, CA Nurses Association, the AFL-CIO, and United Farm Workers. Send her back to Washington to tackle the problems of the nation."

subject.title: US House of Representatives, California District 15

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We are not recommending anyone in this race. Kevin Mullin is a corporate-aligned Congressman and should be pushed by his constituents to back more people-friendly legislation."

subject.title: US House of Representatives, California District 16

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We recommend no candidate in this race. Sam Liccardo is a corporate Democrat and we have no love for corporate types."

subject.title: US House of Representatives, California District 17

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Ro Khanna. We have supported Khanna in the past for his advocacy of Medicare for All, the Green New Deal, debt free college, and his efforts to get corporate PAC money out of elections. In his recent term, Ro has continued to align with our goals by becoming a more outspoken critic of Israel’s genocide, shifting to a position of ending all military aid to Israel (including defensive weapons), has championed Prop 40, and is starting to take the lead on regulating AI by developing an Internet Bill of Rights."

subject.title: US House of Representatives, California District 18

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Zoe Lofgren. Lofgren has been a steady progressive vote in the House for years and has been one of the key tech policy leaders there. We are not thrilled with the fact that she was one of the key figures helping funnel funds into opposing Aisha Wahab in CA-14, so we hope a strong progressive candidate emerges soon to challenge Lofgren."

subject.title: US House of Representatives, California District 19

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We recommend no one here. Jimmy Panetta is a son of the military-industrial complex and we do not need to spend more time or money waging violence on the world."

subject.title: California State Assembly, District 21

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "No recommendation. Diane Papan is a centrist Democrat and we have no interest in supporting her."

subject.title: California State Assembly, District 23

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "No recommendation. Marc Berman is a quintessential moderate who refuses to take meaningful stances to solve homelessness and the housing crisis. We have not supported him in the past and have no intention of doing so for his swan song in the Assembly."

subject.title: California State Assembly, District 24

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend sitting assembly member Alex Lee. While some of Lee’s stances over the past few years have diverged from ours- his opposition to the anti-caste discrimination legislation being one of the more recent incidents- he is still one of the most progressive members of the Assembly and the leading voice on expanding public housing."

subject.title: California State Assembly, District 25

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend sitting assemblymember Ash Kalra. He has been the champion of a state-level single-payer healthcare program for the last half decade, writing several bills to establish Medicare-for-All, including the current version AB-1900. He stood with the Amah Mutsun people in their protection of Juristac (aka Sargent Ranch) near Gilroy and has been a staunch progressive champion in the legislature for years."

subject.title: California State Assembly, District 26

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend the incumbent Patrick Ahrens. As a member of the State Assembly Health Committee, he has been a reliable advocate for universal healthcare coverage for all Californians. Ahrens supports reallocating the budget to remove cost-barriers to higher education by making it more affordable and replicating the successful efforts to allocate funds for affordable housing he spearheaded while president of the Foothill-De Anza Community College District Board."

subject.title: California State Assembly, District 28

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Gail Pellerin. Pellerin is quietly one of the more progressive legislators in the Assembly, receiving a 97/100 from Courage California. There are some concerns with her taking a decent amount of money from law enforcement and real estate PACs, and we hope that she is ready to prioritize housing for people instead of profits for landlords when the votes come up."

subject.title: California State Senate, District 10

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend anyone in this race. Scott Sakakihara is a moderate Democrat and is not going to push for progressive policy. He has a deep background in corporate tech, having worked in Palantir’s finance department and is awash in campaign donations from Uber, Meta, and the cryptocurrency PAC Grow California. He has been a leading voice in expanding the funding and militarization of the Union City police department and is endorsed by the California Association of Realtors. No amount of labor endorsements can erase the fact he is a corporate Democrat."

subject.title: Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District Board, Ward 1

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Ward 1 in the southwestern corner of Santa Clara County is the only competitive seat this year. We are issuing a joint recommendation here for a rare reason: both candidates are really good. Incumbent Craig Gleason is a dedicated public servant with an extensive history of building up and out the open spaces in the Santa Cruz Mountains. Tina Marie To is a marine ecologist and enthusiastic volunteer. She helped facilitate the transition of her childhood community into the Sierra Azul Open Space above Los Gatos. Voters can do no wrong in voting for either candidate."

subject.title: Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District Board, Ward 1

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Ward 1 in the southwestern corner of Santa Clara County is the only competitive seat this year. We are issuing a joint recommendation here for a rare reason: both candidates are really good. Incumbent Craig Gleason is a dedicated public servant with an extensive history of building up and out the open spaces in the Santa Cruz Mountains. Tina Marie To is a marine ecologist and enthusiastic volunteer. She helped facilitate the transition of her childhood community into the Sierra Azul Open Space above Los Gatos. Voters can do no wrong in voting for either candidate."

subject.title: Santa Clara County Board of Education, Trustee Area 7

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "District 7 in the southern part of the county features the only competitive race this year. Running for the board seat are incumbent Raeena Lari and Walsh STEAM Academy employee Karla Dominguez Vega. We recommend Raeena Lari and believe she will win a second term with ease."

subject.title: Santa Clara Valley Water District Board, District 1

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "No recommendation. There is not much information available for either candidate, and what little we have found has not shown much difference between the two candidates. Voters will have to rely on local knowledge when making their choice here."

subject.title: Santa Clara Valley Water District Board, District 6

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "This seat is open as Tony Estremera has hit the term limit. Running to replace him are Phuong Nguyen, one of Sen. Dave Cortese’s staffers, and Milan Balinton, a former Franklin-McKinley district trustee. We recommend Balinton as he has laid out a platform that puts equity and access first."

subject.title: Santa Clara Valley Water District Board, District 7

positions.label: Cautious recommendation
positions.statement: "Rebecca Eisenberg’s conduct during this years-long escapade about a report detailing her behavior towards Valley Water employees makes her unfit to continue to be an elected official. We will give a cautious recommendation to Pete Dailey though. Dailey’s platform is open to the idea that more data centers can be built in the future, a position that the community should be pressuring him to change."

subject.title: Campbell City Council, District 3

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Joseph Brenner for this seat because we generally like his platform vision. Daniel Furtado has served well over the decades, but he is a man who legislates for today. Brenner, with a focus on smart growth, deepening communal ties, and plans to address climate change, make him a legislator for tomorrow."

subject.title: Campbell City Council, District 4

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We recommend no one for this race. We do not see the anti-housing Fields as a good choice for Campbell, but Guardado does not seem to have much of a shot with his shoe-string campaign."

subject.title: Cupertino City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend the slate of J.R. Fruen, John Tang, and Seema Lindskog. Housing development will be coming to Cupertino, with or without the approval of the city council. The anti-housing candidates will only guarantee that state-backed Builder’s Remedy will be the dominant housing solution in Cupertino. These three candidates will work to facilitate housing growth in Cupertino that stays in the hands of the community."

subject.title: Cupertino City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend the slate of J.R. Fruen, John Tang, and Seema Lindskog. Housing development will be coming to Cupertino, with or without the approval of the city council. The anti-housing candidates will only guarantee that state-backed Builder’s Remedy will be the dominant housing solution in Cupertino. These three candidates will work to facilitate housing growth in Cupertino that stays in the hands of the community."

subject.title: Cupertino City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend the slate of J.R. Fruen, John Tang, and Seema Lindskog. Housing development will be coming to Cupertino, with or without the approval of the city council. The anti-housing candidates will only guarantee that state-backed Builder’s Remedy will be the dominant housing solution in Cupertino. These three candidates will work to facilitate housing growth in Cupertino that stays in the hands of the community."

subject.title: East Palo Alto City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "There is a strong field of candidates in East Palo Alto for the two open seats. Ruben Abrica, the incumbent, has been a long term advocate for affordable housing. There are other good choices in the race, but none have the track record that Abrica has established in the last 40 plus years. We also recommend Ofelia Bello. She has been a long term advocate for tenant rights and affordable housing. She seems to have solid support behind her campaign."

subject.title: East Palo Alto City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "There is a strong field of candidates in East Palo Alto for the two open seats. Ruben Abrica, the incumbent, has been a long term advocate for affordable housing. There are other good choices in the race, but none have the track record that Abrica has established in the last 40 plus years. We also recommend Ofelia Bello. She has been a long term advocate for tenant rights and affordable housing. She seems to have solid support behind her campaign."

subject.title: Fremont City Council, District 2

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Desrie Campbell. She has been the lone vote against the homeless encampment ban, she has worked towards affordable housing, and she has emphasized services that help the unhoused in Fremont instead of punishing them. Campbell has also worked on protecting the immigrant community and advancing on climate change policies. This is a candidate that will help the people."

subject.title: Fremont City Council, District 3

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Kathy Kimberlin. Kimberlin had pushed to ensure that the ‘aiding and abetting’ provision in the 2025 camping ordinance was removed to allow nonprofits to be able to help the unhoused population. She has supported refugee resettlement programs, affordable housing programs, and expanding food and shelter for the unhoused."

subject.title: Fremont City Council, District 4

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Aziz Akbari. Although he has not held a seat like the others running in the different districts, he is running on progressive policies, such as protecting immigrant communities by not having local cooperation with ICE, expanding affordable and transit-oriented housing, and enacting stronger renter protections. His record on the Alameda County Water District also includes expanding assistance for low-income households to help keep access to clean water affordable."

subject.title: Gilroy City Council, District 4

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend any candidate in this race. Fred Tovar has voted against transit, against housing, and against renter protections when he was previously in office. There is a preference for Diana Sanchez Bentz as she at least pays lip service to improving services in low-income apartment complexes in Gilroy. However, there is little else to go off of in the way of policy or issues besides her focus on transparency and good governance."

subject.title: Gilroy City Council, District 5

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend any candidate in this race. Tom Cline is the worst choice of the three candidates running. He supports increased policing and is a supporter of the potential Amazon data center in Gilroy. Joseph Garcia is the only candidate in the district whose platform includes calling for capping ‘unfair’ rent increases. He also is the only candidate of the three to express skepticism around the new data center. As such, he is likely the safest choice, despite not having a well developed platform or track record to go off of. Christina Tovar seems to be business oriented and also is lacking in policy proposals."

subject.title: Gilroy City Council, District 6

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Rebeca Armendariz. Armendariz has been a steady progressive voice on the council. She has been active in organizing against ICE and has fought for racial and economic justice in Gilroy. She is the clear choice in the race."

subject.title: Los Altos City Council, District 2

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Los Altos is having its first district elections this year, with the new 2nd District being the one competitive race this year. Two candidates have filed to run for this seat and we recommend voters choose Anky van Deursen for the seat. van Deursen is a Housing Manager for the City of Mountain View and sits on Los Altos’ Rent Stabilization Commission. Her campaign priorities are housing for service workers, an emphasis on quality of living for retirees, and more kid/bike safe streets. Lynette Lee Eng is a disgraced former councilmember who was pressured to resign after accusing a black resident of threatening her family over BLM discussions in 2021. Her platform priorities are vaguely about ‘governing with respect and integrity.’"

subject.title: Los Gatos Town Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Rob Moore and Jeff Suzuki. Moore is a knowledgeable leader and has been a good steward of the Los Gatos community the last four years. Suzuki’s history of activism and policy knowledge ensure that equity and justice will always be at the forefront of his policies."

subject.title: Los Gatos Town Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Rob Moore and Jeff Suzuki. Moore is a knowledgeable leader and has been a good steward of the Los Gatos community the last four years. Suzuki’s history of activism and policy knowledge ensure that equity and justice will always be at the forefront of his policies."

subject.title: Menlo Park City Council, District 1

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend any candidate in this race. Neither candidate has staked out positions that set each apart in a meaningful way. Wonman Lee might be the slightly better choice, if only because he has the clearest messaging and appears to recognize the problem of NIMBYism in Menlo Park."

subject.title: Menlo Park City Council, District 2

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend any candidate in this race. Neither candidate stands apart here. Drew Combs, the incumbent, has been on the wrong side of the housing debate on the council at times. His opponent, Velgapudi, seems to be running primarily because he doesn’t like the way things are done at city council meetings. He has not been able to articulate a reason that he warrants a vote."

subject.title: Menlo Park City Council, District 4

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Charlotte Reed. While she does not have a proven record, her position on affordable housing in downtown Menlo Park puts her well ahead of her venture capitalist opponent, Laura Melahn. Melahn was unwilling to take a position on development of housing in downtown."

subject.title: Milpitas Mayor

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Hon Lien. Lien’s record includes expanding affordable housing, preserving housing for low-income residents, and providing resources and services to unhoused people. She has advocated direct public support of the Milpitas Food Pantry, proposing $5,000 per month in city funding for two years to help it continue providing food and assistance to families, seniors, veterans, and other residents in need."

subject.title: Milpitas City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend only Seema Kanani in this race. Kanani served on the executive board of SEIU-UHW, and while she was in this capacity she helped organize during the 2023 Kaiser strike that secured significant wage increases for healthcare workers. She also advocated for protecting immigrant patients and making housing more affordable for working families, seniors, and lower-income residents."

subject.title: Morgan Hill Mayor

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend any candidate in this race. Incumbent Mark Turner is a business- aligned moderate, while the two candidates also running, Debora Africa and Kristopher Clayton, do not have backgrounds or policy positions that set them apart in any meaningful way."

subject.title: Morgan Hill City Council, District B

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend any candidate in this race. The incumbent Yvonne Martinez Beltran is a moderate Democrat. She has recently run into trouble with fellow council members for her inflammatory comments. Despite that, her opponent - Steven Hayes - does not really present a distinct platform warranting serious consideration."

subject.title: Morgan Hill City Council, District D

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Dolores Alvarado. She is endorsed by several labor organizations and a slate of progressive local leaders. Her incumbent opponent Marilyn Libers has for years opposed large housing developments in the city. Alvarado is the clear choice in this race."

subject.title: Mountain View City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Erik Poicon, IdaRose Sylvester, and James Kuszmaul. All three are local progressive organizers running on affordable housing growth to stave off Builder’s Remedy and empowering downtown to continue to thrive."

subject.title: Mountain View City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Erik Poicon, IdaRose Sylvester, and James Kuszmaul. All three are local progressive organizers running on affordable housing growth to stave off Builder’s Remedy and empowering downtown to continue to thrive."

subject.title: Mountain View City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Erik Poicon, IdaRose Sylvester, and James Kuszmaul. All three are local progressive organizers running on affordable housing growth to stave off Builder’s Remedy and empowering downtown to continue to thrive."

subject.title: Newark City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend incumbent Matthew Jorgens. Jorgens is a bonafide progressive with a very detailed platform that balances the needs to grow as a city and the wants of the community to keep their small-town feel."

subject.title: Palo Alto City Council

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Raymond Goins. Palo Alto needs progressive voices on the council and the current batch of neoliberals jostling for the 3 seats are underwhelming. Goins is an outspoken critic of increased policing and surveillance and will work to represent the underserved communities in Palo Alto."

subject.title: San Jose City Council, District 5

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Peter Ortiz. Ortiz has served as a champion for East San Jose, advocating for and delivering new investments into the arts, housing, education, and parks for District 5. He continues to lead in his community and the community, in turn, supports him. In contrast, Campos is part of the business-wing alliance that has propped up her and her family in the district for years."

subject.title: San Jose City Council, District 7

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend either candidate. Bien Doan and Van Le have very little difference in their policy platforms and politics, meaning that both candidates will be aligned with the business faction on the city council."

subject.title: San Jose City Council, District 9

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Gordon Chester. Chester is a city civil engineer and understands the need to invest in public infrastructure and not back away from expanding public transit. He also will work to curtail the overbloated police budget and reinvest those funds back into community safety programs, something we doubt former cop Altwer will do."

subject.title: Santa Clara Mayor

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend a candidate in this race. Kevin Park, current councilmember has been strong against ICE, ALPRs and Data Centers, but has had an uncomfortably close past with 49ers ownership. Karen Hardy shares the 49ers issue, but lacks the bonafides of Park and is conservative. Gary Ferraris, while having some labor group backing, is a conservative as well as being the 49ers’ dedicated pick. David Kertes and Kathy Watanabe have been strong opponents of the 49ers, but have a close relationship to Mayor Lisa Gillmor and the established business community. On top of that Kertes has personal baggage such as a failed recall attempt to replace a current councilmember."

subject.title: Santa Clara City Council, District 2

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend either candidate. Yvonne Inciarte and Kimberley Williams do not have much variety in their platforms, meaning that both candidates will have a similar impact on the City Council if elected. Williams seems to be the 49ers pick."

subject.title: Santa Clara City Council, District 3

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We do not recommend either candidate. Eric Crutchlow is the current City Planning Commission Chair campaigning on limiting council meeting lengths, which seems a dangerous tool to allow bypassing public input. Kyle Madej is a private security CEO running on increasing police funding and little else."

subject.title: Union City City Council, District 2

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Victor Pulido for this seat. Pulido is a community organizer and Human Relations commissioner who is advocating for municipal food stores, renter protections, and investments into the working families of Union City. We couldn’t agree more."

subject.title: Union City City Council, District 3

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Cheris Crocker-Root. Jeff Wang is a rarity in the Bay Area- an elected Republican. By extension, he is inherently okay with the anti-human agenda of his party and should not be near any lever of power. Crocker-Root will at least work to address the root causes of problems instead of just kvetch about the ills of society."

subject.title: Union City City Council, District 4

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "This is the most crowded and weakest field of candidates in Union City elections this year. Bajwa and Lodhi are business-aligned moderates who will not solve the problems of today with adequacy. Yap-Jequinto is a good person without a plan. That leaves us to recommend teacher Sarabjit Cheema, who at least has decent plans to address housing and development."

subject.title: Foothill-De Anza Community College District Board, Trustee Area 4

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Bill Wilson. Wilson is a Foothill professor and is endorsed by the rest of trustees and the South Bay Labor Council."

subject.title: San José-Evergreen Community College District Board, Trustee Area 2

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "We recommend no one for this race. Incumbent Karen Martinez is a pro-police moderate and not of our liking. Meanwhile, Scott Pham abandoned his seat before getting sworn in when he was elected to the Alum Rock Union board of trustees."

subject.title: West Valley-Mission Community College District Board, Trustee Area 3

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We are giving a joint recommendation here. Incumbent Anne Kepner is a progressive leader and has been advocating to make tuition free for the two colleges. Colin Glaves is backed by faculty and is advocating for more teacher-board coordination. Both candidates are also endorsed by the South Bay Labor Council."

subject.title: West Valley-Mission Community College District Board, Trustee Area 3

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We are giving a joint recommendation here. Incumbent Anne Kepner is a progressive leader and has been advocating to make tuition free for the two colleges. Colin Glaves is backed by faculty and is advocating for more teacher-board coordination. Both candidates are also endorsed by the South Bay Labor Council."

subject.title: West Valley-Mission Community College District Board, Trustee Area 7

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Doug Robb, who is endorsed by the faculty union and the South Bay Labor Council."

subject.title: East Side Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 1 (Short Term)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Meredith ‘Mer’ Nunez. Nunez has a minimal platform, but a long history of advocacy and work to indicate that she is ready to tackle the problems facing education these days."

subject.title: East Side Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 4

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend incumbent Lorena Chavez. Chavez has plans to continue to build off the good work she has done in office already and is endorsed by loads of local progressives."

subject.title: Fremont Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 3

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Rosa Kim. Kim is a perfectly fine trustee and we don’t trust serial tech entrepreneur Lin to oversee a public sector board."

subject.title: Fremont Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 4

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We are going with a joint recommendation here. Naomi Nakano-Matsumoto is a veteran trustee who has done a lot to help the district. Ilanit Eliaz is a special education teacher who could bring a unique view to the board and has won a lot of local support. Voters are lucky to have two solid candidates to choose from."

subject.title: Fremont Union High School District Board, Trustee Area 4

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We are going with a joint recommendation here. Naomi Nakano-Matsumoto is a veteran trustee who has done a lot to help the district. Ilanit Eliaz is a special education teacher who could bring a unique view to the board and has won a lot of local support. Voters are lucky to have two solid candidates to choose from."

subject.title: Gilroy Unified School District Board, Trustee Area 3

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend incumbent Michelle Nelson. Nelson is a union leader and health teacher and has served as a good liaison between the workers and the district."

subject.title: Gilroy Unified School District Board, Trustee Area 4

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Jane Stevens for this seat as she has a decent platform and the backing of the Gilroy Teachers Association."

subject.title: Milpitas Unified School District Board

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend Chris Norwood. Norwood backs the Workforce Development Center in the district, a great community resource for connecting students with local jobs."

subject.title: Morgan Hill Unified School District Board, Trustee Area 1

positions.label: Recommended

subject.title: California — Proposition 1 (Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We urge a Yes vote on Prop 1. It authorizes a $11.25 billion bond that is focused on adding and preserving affordable housing. It also assists veterans and attempts to create longer lasting programs for the unhoused population. The funds are necessary, given the current housing and affordability crises throughout the state."

subject.title: California — Proposition 2 (Increases State's Rainy Day Fund)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We urge a Yes vote on this proposition. It is a straightforward increase of the percentage of the budget the state is allowed to keep in the Rainy Day Fund. In years where there is an economic surplus, California could put double the amount of money into savings. In turn, that money could be spent on services and programs during an economic downturn. The state’s ability to do that is currently limited by the percentage limitation and this proposition fixes that."

subject.title: California — Proposition 3 (Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes)

positions.label: Endorsed
positions.statement: "Silicon Valley DSA endorses a Yes vote on Prop 3. The Children’s Education and Health Care Protection Act would make permanent the temporary income tax imposed on the top 2% of income earners by Proposition 55 in 2016. This tax raised $14 billion last year for public education and health care. The loss of that funding would be catastrophic."

subject.title: California — Proposition 4 (Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "This measure would lift the statewide ban on public financing of campaigns and allow the state and local governments to establish programs that grant public funds to supplement campaigns. Public campaign financing is used across multiple states and municipalities, including New York City, Seattle, San Francisco, and Oakland. These systems have been proven to boost corporate-free candidates for office and blunt some of the effects of wealthy corporations and the uber-rich spending millions in local elections. We urge voters to vote Yes on this measure to continue to fight back against the monied forces rigging our democracy."

subject.title: California — Proposition 5 (Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers)

positions.label: Neutral
positions.statement: "We are neutral on this measure. Separating the recall election from the recall question is a better use of election resources, and having the Lt. Governor take over for a recalled governor makes sense. What we are leery about is the second reform, allowing a recalled officer to run in the special election created by their removal. If someone is so unpopular that they are recalled, that is a reflection of popular opinion. Allowing that recalled official to run again in an election where we use a plurality system instead of a majoritarian system like ranked choice voting means that there is a chance the recalled official wins, a defiance to democratic choice- and a waste of everyone’s time and public resources."

subject.title: California — Proposition 37 (Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "This homebuyer program and bond initiative is being funded by the same billionaires trying to stop Prop 40 - Sergey Brin and his cynically named ‘Building a Better California’ PAC. It’s also funded by his friends in real estate and construction, and endorsed by a number of corrupt politicians. We recommend a No vote on this measure. Any potential upfront benefit only obscures the costs and intentions of this measure. New home buyers are locked into a program with imperfect information. One thing is certain, this will create more debt, which benefits the home builders and real estate firms which are intentionally financializing homes into assets. Homes are for living in - they’re a human necessity. Follow the money."

subject.title: California — Proposition 38 (Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "This measure would issue $8.4 billion in bonds for immunotherapy and immunology research. The money would be split evenly between a UC-affiliated research institute and non-profit research institutes focused on immunology research. While we like scientific research, we recommend a No vote on this measure. CalMatters found that the measure was written to benefit only one institute, the California Institute for Immunology and Immunotherapy. CIII is founded and funded primarily by billionaire Gary Michelson. Michelson is the one who authored Prop 38, and- along with billionaire Meyer Luskin of Scope Industries- is the primary funder of the Yes campaign. We should not be subsidizing the projects of the uber-rich, regardless if they are corporate aligned or non-profit aligned."

subject.title: California — Proposition 39 (Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "This measure would institute new voter id laws and a more aggressive voter roll monitoring system. We recommend No on this measure. California already has a secure end-to-end system to check people’s identities when they register and vote. This measure is designed to disenfranchise voters and intimidate people unnecessarily. Most alarming is the requirement to put parts of your government id on mail-in ballots, a massive privacy threat."

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.label: Endorsed
positions.statement: "Silicon Valley DSA endorses a Yes vote on Prop 40. We need to fund healthcare, not continue to allow the ultra-rich to buy ever more mansions and yachts, and invest in job-killing AI. It’s time to tax the rich. The 2026 Billionaire Tax Act would levy a one-time 5% wealth tax on individuals worth more than $1 billion in order to offset the loss of almost $100 billion in federal funding for Medi-Cal. Without this funding, thousands of jobs will be lost, millions of Californians could lose coverage altogether, and care facilities across the state could be forced to close. The billionaires have spent over $150 million against Prop 40. They have also funded two competing ballot measures, Prop 41 & Prop 42. For Prop 40 to become law, it must receive more votes than both Prop 41 & Prop 42. People will die if we do not pass Prop 40, therefore it is a no-brainer to vote Yes on Prop 40."

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.label: Endorsed
positions.statement: "Silicon Valley DSA endorses a NO vote on Prop 41, and highly encourages everyone to vote down this cynical, billionaire-funded bill. Follow the money! Billionaires like Sergei Brin, John Doerr, Peter Thiel, Chris Larsen, Eric Schmidt, and Stuart Resnick have spent well over $150 million on competing ballot measures aimed at preventing the implementation of Prop 40. As a competing ballot measure, for Prop 40 (the ‘billionaire tax’) to become law, it must receive more votes than BOTH Prop 41 & 42. People will die if we do not pass Prop 40, therefore it is a no-brainer to vote no on Prop 41."

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.label: Endorsed
positions.statement: "Silicon Valley DSA also endorses a NO vote on Prop 42, and highly encourages everyone to vote down this cynical, billionaire-funded bill. This is the second of two competing ballot measures aimed at preventing the implementation of Prop 40. These billionaires will stop at nothing to prevent us from taking back a crumb of the wealth they have stolen from regular people. They know preventing Prop 40 from becoming law will mean the closing of dozens hospitals, hundreds of healthcare professionals losing their jobs, and the deaths of tens of thousands of our fellow Californians who will lose coverage because Trump took $100 billion in healthcare funding from California, to give tax cuts to his billionaire friends. Prop 42 is written by, and is in service to the worst people in society - the billionaire class. As a competing ballot measure, for Prop 40 (the ‘billionaire tax’) to become law, it must receive more votes than Prop 41 & Prop 42. People will die if we do not pass Prop 40, therefore it is a no-brainer to vote no on Prop 42."

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "This measure would require a two-thirds vote by the electorate to enact, extend, or increase local special tax initiatives and prohibit local jurisdictions and ballot initiatives from enacting ad valorem property taxes, except for voter-approved bond debt-service taxes authorized elsewhere in the state constitution. We will be recommending No on this measure. Evolve California warns 'if this measure passes, it will make California the hardest place in the country to raise local revenue.' With the federal government increasingly threatening the funding of our public services, we cannot let anti-tax sentiments choke out the last of our public services."

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.label: No recommendation
positions.statement: "No recommendation. The nonprofit federally qualified health centers this measure is directed at do need some more regulation and oversight, particularly in not meddling with unionization efforts. However, using the ballot initiative process as a negotiation tactic, which SEIU-UHW has done several times before, does not garner positive relations with the public and should not be condoned."

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "This measure would shorten deadlines and environmental reviews for a number of infrastructure projects in California by making changes to the California Environmental Quality Act and the Permit Streamlining Act. We will be recommending No on this measure. The CEQA does need some adjusting and 21st century modernizing, but to rely on a corporate authored measure like Prop 45 is stupendously detrimental."

subject.title: Gilroy — Measure B

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure B would increase Gilroy’s Transient Occupancy Tax (hotel tax) to the maximum rate of 13% to fund weather emergency preparedness, fire/police, and park/street infrastructure. Gilroy has one of the highest per capita homelessness rates in the Bay Area, nearly double that of San Jose. Considering the large unhoused/underhoused population that rely on these rooms, such a tax would hit these already struggling residents the hardest. We recommend voting No."

subject.title: Los Altos — Measure D (Citizen-Sponsored Initiative)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure D would prohibit Los Altos from selling/leasing/donating downtown parking plazas without a ballot measure. The Measure has former mayors, council members, and park commissioners on both sides of the argument. The main argument is to prevent commercial development that city parking infrastructure can’t handle (especially if diminished by development). While the language does imply that housing would be exempted from such a ballot measure, the City Attorney’s Impartial Analysis states that this is not the case and highlights that YIMBY Law Group is threatening a future court case. We recommend voting No."

subject.title: Redwood City — Measure E (Rent Control and Eviction Limits Initiative)

positions.label: Endorsed
positions.statement: "Silicon Valley DSA is proud to endorse Yes on Measure E. This measure would implement rent control on certain residential rentals in Redwood City and provide more protections for renters. Housing for all means ensuring that people can afford to stay in their homes and not end up on the street. Vote Yes to keep people homed in Redwood City."

subject.title: Mountain View — Measure F (Transient Occupancy Tax)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure F permits the Mountain View city council to raise the hotel tax upwards to 15% from its current rate of 10%. Generated revenue would go to the city’s General Fund. We recommend voting Yes on this measure. Mountain View is close to Levi’s Stadium and the tech titans, meaning that the majority of the tax burden will fall on wealthy travelers and not on the people of Mountain View, an ideal progressive tax."

subject.title: Palo Alto — Measure J (Transactions and Use Tax)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure J is a 0.5% sales tax aiming to raise ~$15 million for purchasing 7 acres from Palo Alto Unified School District to expand and renovate Cubberley Community Center. The Palo Alto City Council voted unanimously to put this Measure on the ballot. The opponents of the measure (spearheaded by anti-tax groups and former mayor Lydia Kou) state that the taxes raised are not required to go to the stated purpose of purchasing and renovating the community center. The City Attorney concurs with them in their analysis, but also states that the City has historically honored spending guidelines such as the one passed specifying the funds go to Cubberley. We recommend voting Yes."

subject.title: San Mateo County — Measure J (Charter Amendment Measure – Extension to Call a Special Election or Appoint)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure J for San Mateo County extends the period required for the County Board of Supervisors to call an election or make an appointment in event of a vacancy from 30 to 60 days, and also requires the board to conduct one public comment session prior to appointment. We recommend voting Yes."

subject.title: Milpitas — Measure K

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure K would impose a ~0.025%-0.035% gross receipt tax on businesses with greater than $700,000 in annual revenue. This plans to raise roughly $3 million annually for city finances and neighborhood infrastructure. Opposition to the measure is largely spearheaded by the anti-tax Silicon Valley Taxpayers Association. We recommend voting Yes."

subject.title: Cupertino — Measure L

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure L would require a two-thirds vote by Cupertino voters to authorize rezoning of parks, parklands, or open spaces to residential, commercial, or industrial zones. This is overwhelmingly supported by ~70% of Cupertino residents surveyed in June. We recommend voting Yes. Part of making the Bay Area a livable area is to pair amenities with housing. This includes keeping our current parklands as parks and building dense housing near them, not on them."

subject.title: East Palo Alto — Measure O (Bond Measure)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure O would impose a 1.5% tax on revenue of owners who lease 5+ units in EPA to raise ~600k in funds for local services. There are certain exceptions for Section 8/below market housing, and only units which have had a certificate of occupancy for 10+ years are counted. This was passed 4-1 by their city council and had no organized opposition. It is largely popular with residents. We recommend voting Yes."

subject.title: Menlo Park — Measure P (Citizen Initiative to Amend Municipal Code)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure P would prohibit Menlo Park from selling/leasing/donating city-owned land if it would reduce parking availability without a voter measure. This is spearheaded by Alex Beltramo, a local business owner who wants to ensure existing parking lots for Menlo Park’s commercial downtown on Santa Cruz Ave is not developed into parking structures with affordable housing on top. We recommend voting No."

subject.title: El Camino Healthcare District — Measure S

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure S amends the El Camino Healthcare District bylaws to limit district directors to four 4-year terms. Currently there are no term limits. We recommend voting Yes."

subject.title: San Mateo County — Measure U (Charter Amendment Measure – Reapportionment of Supervisorial Districts)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure U would change San Mateo County’s districting process from an ordinance approved by the Board of Supervisors to a redrawn-each-decade by independent commission process. The independent commission would be elected by district. We recommend voting Yes."

subject.title: East Palo Alto — Measure CC (Term Limits Measure)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure CC imposes a three consecutive term limit on city council members, with a partial term of 2+ years counting as a full term. We recommend voting Yes."

subject.title: Newark — Measure DD (Newark Essential Services Protection Measure)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure DD would implement a business tax increase of up to 0.3% on gross receipts to raise an estimated $6 million annually to fund police/fire services, street infrastructure, and weather emergency preparedness. The tax restructuring would also lower taxes for smaller businesses. The City Attorney notes in their independent analysis that the city is not bound to use the funds for the stated purpose as long as they are used to support city services. Proponents say 87% of local retail businesses will pay lower business license taxes under this restructuring. Opposition, led by Council Member Terrence Grindall claims the taxes will be passed on to residents through price increases. We recommend voting Yes."

subject.title: Union City — Measure II (Union City Essential Services Extension Measure)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "Measure II would extend the existing Utility Users Tax at the current rate of 5% for another 9 years, raising an estimated $7m annually. The stated intent for the funds is for funding emergency response systems, street infrastructure, and violence prevention programs but as with other similar measures it is a general tax which the city is not bound to use for those purposes as long as it is spent for local services.The measure would also continue the allowance of exceptions for 70+ year old as well as low income residents, and continue the existing audits of the collection and expenditures by a third party. The only opposition seems to come from Alameda County Taxpayers’ Association. We recommend voting Yes."

subject.title: Bay Area — Regional Measure RTM (Regional Transit Measure)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "We recommend you vote Yes. If we don’t approve this critical funding measure, everyday people will face longer, more expensive commutes. Transit services across the Bay Area will be slashed by up to 70%, leading to closed stations, longer waits, and abandoned routes. While a sales tax is not our favored method, it’s unfortunately the only legal option at this time."

subject.title: Gilroy Unified School District — Measure M (School Bonds)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "These measures are for issuing bonds or renewing parcel taxes in school districts across Santa Clara and San Mateo Counties. We recognize that the way these measures generate funds are not the best way to fund our education system and that these are ultimately regressive and affect everyday people more so than the rich or business communities. However, given how undersupported our education funding is in California, these measures are the only viable ways to maintain current school funding. We recommend that everybody vote Yes on their local measure, then call your state assemblymember and senator to have them work on ways to fully fund our public education systems."

subject.title: Alum Rock Union Elementary School District — Measure P (General Obligation Bond)

positions.label: Recommended
positions.statement: "These measures are for issuing bonds or renewing parcel taxes in school districts across Santa Clara and San Mateo Counties. We recognize that the way these measures generate funds are not the best way to fund our education system and that these are ultimately regressive and affect everyday people more so than the rich or business communities. However, given how undersupported our education funding is in California, these measures are the only viable ways to maintain current school funding. We recommend that everybody vote Yes on their local measure, then call your state assemblymember and senator to have them work on ways to fully fund our public education systems."
